ops.title: os.Rename over a running Mach-O succeeds on APFS; proc_pidpath still returns the path
ops.body:
Measured 2026-08-01 by the P4.2a refuter, running the primitive rather than reasoning about it
(scratch test in internal/proc, since deleted):

- `os.Rename` over a currently-executing Mach-O **succeeds** on APFS. The running process survives
  on its old inode.
- `proc_pidpath` on that process still returns the (now replaced) path — it does NOT answer ENOENT.

Consequence for the absence gate: `ExecutableIdentities(stablePath)` reports an old daemon whose
bytes were replaced under it as **Matched**, not Unnameable. The ENOENT arm at
`internal/proc/executable.go:87` — and therefore the `KERN_PROCARGS2` fallback in
`execPathFromArgs` — never fires for this case.

This corrects a mechanism claim made during P4.2a: the stable program path was argued to *improve*
the absence gate because `proc_pidpath` would ENOENT on an unlinked text vnode and the harness would
recover the path from `KERN_PROCARGS2`. The conclusion (the old daemon stays visible to the gate)
holds; the stated mechanism does not — it is visible because `proc_pidpath` simply works.

The ENOENT arm still has a real trigger (a genuinely unlinked, not replaced, executable) — this note
narrows what it covers, it does not make it dead code.

Related: [[program-path-stable-wins-staged-is-strictly-dominated]].
